statements.text: Recently, the Commerce Department issued rules that require U.S. chipmakers to attain a license in order to export AI chips. [...] I believe this is on the right track, you know, protecting the United States from global adversaries is a bipartisan nonnegotiable issue.
statements.context: House hearing on AI data and innovation, featuring Member questions to an expert panel.

statements.text: At the same time, the Chinese Communist Party is moving fast and hard with zero regulations and zero ethical restraints, so we have our work cut out for us.
statements.context: Opening statement at a hearing on AI technology, human discovery, and American global competitiveness.

statements.text: We focused on AI regulations, regulations on AI labeling, watermarking standards, harmful risks such as deepfakes, fraud prevention, cybersecurity protocols, et cetera.
statements.context: Opening statement by Rep. Dunn at a House subcommittee hearing on AI applications in communications and technology.

statements.text: Mr. Shea, you spoke about U.S. leadership in AI, and DeepSig's tech, like your AI-native wireless capabilities, coupled with Open RAN networks will reduce costs to replace custom hardware and allow us to better compete with China and whatnot, specifically Huawei. Can you elaborate on your company's vision, how you see that entrepreneurship leading to the conversations, but also the actions of the companies in creating new technologies?
statements.context: Exchange between Mr. Dunn and a company witness at a hearing on AI applications in communications and technology.

statements.text: Yeah, I was concerned about that, too. So are there, again, Mr. Mahnken, any strategically destabilizing red lines, things that we should be absolutely watching out for in the Chinese AI world?
statements.context: House hearing titled 'Algorithms and Authoritarians: Why U.S. AI Must Lead' on June 25, 2025.

statements.text: Dr. Mr. Mahnken, what are the major strategic missteps you think that Congress might make that would be a terrible mistake in the AGI world?
statements.context: Representative Dunn questions a witness at a hearing titled 'Algorithms and Authoritarians: Why U.S. AI Must Lead.'

statements.text: In fact, in this experiment, and I emphasized it was an experiment, Claude attempted to blackmail the chief engineer with damning information he believed to be true. It made no apparent effort to verify the information. It just used it. This is a disturbing scenario to people like me. I don't pretend to be among the cognizanti, but the idea that my computer could turn on me and use my banking data or whatever else it had is concerning.
statements.context: Congressman Dunn questions a witness during a House hearing on U.S. AI leadership, citing an AI experiment described in a newsletter.
